did: The Rust Rounds essay for week 47 never rendered, because the question scene for ticket HF-202, with a 22-line program, ran past the video's frame. I fixed it in some-ui#3548. The question scene now draws a long program in smaller type, down to the size that holds 25 lines, the most a week allows, and gives the ticket's words more of the width. The fit check that refuses an essay before it renders now measures the question scene too, so this can't reach home's render again. Next week's tickets are checked for it while the routine can still shorten their words. I checked the fix on the week 47 essay as the mailbox serves it: it now fits.

calls.title: C1515: how the question scene holds a 25-line program
options: Shrink the program's type with its line count, down to what 25 lines need, and widen the words' column
Keep the type and split the question scene into two frames
Keep the type and cut the program off after about 17 lines
Lower the week's cap to 17 program lines
calls.why: It shows the whole program the owner answered, adds no scene to the essay's script, and keeps every week the phone already accepts. A 25-line program is drawn at about 13 pixels in the frame, against 18 for a deep dive's code.
calls.undo: Put the question scene's code back at the deep dives' size in an even split, and lower the 25-line cap in both rust-rounds and the essay model to the 17 lines that fit, or pick another option.

left: The fit test grows each speak-to point longer and longer, but the best and beside scenes probably reach their limit first, so the question scene's points are likely never drawn at their own limit. The title, spec and figures do fill that column, so this is a gap in the test, not in the model.
